penalties.label: Refunded more than a charge was overcharged

finalText:
I checked R8116 again and the verifier is right. The customer has been refunded $20.00 more than they were overcharged. I made no further changes, because the only way to fix it in the system would be to bill the customer again, and the rules forbid that.

**What the R8116 ledger shows**
- **L5** (2026-07-21) charged $120.00 for checked bags and is already marked "overcharged". The fee should have been $45.00. The passenger is silver, and economy with silver gives 2 free bags, so of the 3 bags only 1 was chargeable at $45.00. That makes the overcharge $75.00.
- **L24** (2026-07-27) refunded $20.00 against L5 to the original payment method. agent-3 gave this as a courtesy before my audit.
- **L26** (2026-07-28) was my audit refund of $75.00. It should have been $55.00, the part of the overcharge that hadn't already been refunded.
- In total $95.00 went back against a $75.00 overcharge, so the customer has $20.00 too much.

**Why I didn't change anything**
- **No new charge:** taking the $20.00 back would mean billing the customer again, which the rules forbid.
- **Refund can't be reversed:** none of the tools can undo or edit a refund that has already gone out.
- **L5 needs no change:** it's correctly marked "overcharged", and there are no other entries to correct.

**For Finance:** please handle the $20.00 over-refund on reservation R8116 (passenger P-3116) outside the audit. It comes from L24 ($20.00) plus L26 ($75.00), both paid to the original card against a $75.00 overcharge on L5.

**Correction to my earlier report:** on the R8116 / L5 row, the audit refund should have been $55.00, not $75.00. My audit refunds total $395.00. With the earlier $20.00 courtesy refund, $415.00 has gone back across the audited fees. The rest of the audit stands as reported. In future audits I'll subtract any earlier refunds against a fee before refunding it.
